summary: Clozel and Thorne prove that the 6th and 8th symmetric powers of a non-CM cuspidal representation π of GL_2(A_F) attached to a Hilbert modular form exist, for F totally real and linearly disjoint from Q(ζ_5), resp. Q(ζ_7) (Theorem 6.1). With their earlier papers and a reduction for forms of mixed parity (§7) this gives Sym^n π for n ≤ 8 when F ∩ Q(ζ_35) = Q (Corollary 7.2), and the holomorphy of L(Sym^n π, s). The key is the congruence Sym^{l+1} r̄ ≅ (φr̄ ⊗ r̄) ⊕ χ²Sym^{l−3} r̄ for l = 5, 7: the residual representation is endoscopic of type (4, l − 2), so a Steinberg lift of it must be produced before Thorne's automorphy lifting for residually reducible representations applies. They construct Iwahori-spherical representations of ramified unitary groups by Kazhdan–Lusztig, place them in Mœglin–Mok L-packets and study their integral structures (§§2–3). They count automorphic representations of a definite unitary group with endoscopic base change (Theorem 3.8), raise the level with algebraic modular forms and a pairing argument that works only for l = 5, 7 (Theorem 4.2), and raise it further to Steinberg by deformation theory of reducible residual representations (Theorem 5.1, giving the automorphy lifting Theorem 5.7). In the atlas the endpoints belong to ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.3, which receives the final theorems and the §7 reductions as a source route. The level-raising method is planned nowhere and becomes a Part II of that roadmap. Casselman's lemma, the Iwahori–Matsumoto and Bernstein–Lusztig presentations and Kazhdan–Lusztig go as sources to SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1–SR.3, and the partition deformation rings R^m_v to LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7. Mok's classification (ML.4), the known transfers (ML.5), unitary trace formulas (ET.4/ET.7), buildings (RG2.2/RG2.4) and the attached Galois representations (AG2.x) are planned. Five misprints are recorded; no stated result is affected.

items.name: Existence of the n-th symmetric power lift Sym^n π
items.statement: Let F be a totally real field and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(A_F) attached to a classical Hilbert modular form (weights ≥ 2, constant parity) that is not of CM type. Sym^n π exists if there is a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL_{n+1}(A_F) with Sym^n r_l(π) ≅ r_l(Π) for every prime l (for one, hence every, embedding of the coefficient field into Q̄_l); for mixed-parity π (§7) the condition is Sym^n rec_{F_v}(π_v) ≅ rec_{F_v}(Π_v) at every finite place v.
items.note: ML.0 plans the endpoint and normalisation registry and ML.3 the symmetric-power endpoints; this Galois-theoretic definition is the form of the endpoint the Clozel–Thorne series proves.

items.name: Conventions of [CT14, §2]: RACSDC, RAESDC and RACSD representations, ι-ordinarity, weight and infinity type, and r_ι(π)
items.statement: For a CM or totally real field, regular algebraic (essentially) conjugate self-dual cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n (RACSDC, RAESDC, RAECSDC, RACSD), the weight λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(E,C)} and infinity type a of a regular algebraic cuspidal representation, ι-ordinarity for ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, the local Langlands correspondences rec_{F_v}, rec^T_{F_v} for GL_n, the attached Galois representations r_ι(π): G_F → GL_n(Q̄_l), and what it means for a Galois representation to be automorphic.
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.0 plans weights and normalisations and AG2.2 the polarized Galois systems; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.2 the ordinary GL_n theory over CM fields; EndoscopicTransfer ET.6 the local Langlands correspondence for GL_n.

items.name: Galois representations attached to RACSDC representations, with local–global compatibility including monodromy
items.statement: For a RACSDC automorphic representation Π of GL_n(A_E) (E CM) and ι: Q̄_l ≅ C there is a continuous semisimple r_ι(Π): G_E → GL_n(Q̄_l) with r_ι(Π)^c ≅ r_ι(Π)^∨ ε^{1−n}, and for every finite place w ∤ l, WD(r_ι(Π)|_{G_{E_w}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T_{E_w}(Π_w) (Taylor–Yoshida), used with the Jordan decomposition of the monodromy operator N.
items.locator: Used in Proposition 4.1, p. 34, Theorem 5.1, p. 37, and Theorem 5.7, p. 44
items.note: AG2.5 plans 'the Caraiani/Taylor–Yoshida upgrades' with full monodromy comparison.

items.name: The ramified unitary group U_n, its building and the parahoric subgroups B ⊃ Iwahori and P
items.statement: Let p be odd, F/Q_p finite, E/F ramified quadratic with uniformiser ϖ, ϖ² ∈ F, v(ϖ) = ½, n = 2k + 1, and U_n(R) = {g ∈ GL_n(R ⊗_{O_F} O_E) : ᵗg J g^c = J} with J antidiagonal. The maximal split torus S has non-reduced relative root system BC_k; Z = Z_{U_n}(S), Λ = Z/Z_c ≅ Z^k with basis ε_1, …, ε_k. The standard apartment, affine roots {a_ij + ½Z} ∪ {a_i + ½Z} ∪ {2a_i + ½ + Z}, the chamber C: 0 < a_k < ⋯ < a_1 < ¼ with simple affine roots α_0 = 2a_{−1} + ½, a_{1,−2}, …, a_k, and the affine Weyl group W = W_0 ⋉ Λ of type B_k generated by s_0, …, s_k (with s_0 given by (2.1)). K = U_n(O_F) is special; B = U_n^C is the preimage of the upper-triangular subgroup of O(J)(k_F) and contains an Iwahori subgroup with index 2; P = U_n^F is the preimage of block upper-triangular matrices with a 3 × 3 middle block, [P : B] = q + 1. (U_n, B, N) is a Tits system.
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2 plans Bruhat–Tits buildings with facets and fixers, and RG2.4 the Iwahori–Bruhat decomposition with non-split examples. Tau Ceti has the abstract Tits system (TauCeti.TitsSystem, TauCeti/GroupTheory/TitsSystem/Basic.lean:48) and its Bruhat decomposition, but not buildings or parahorics. Corrected for source issue E1 (the paper prints Λ ≅ Z^m).

items.name: Lemma 2.1: invariants of B and P through Jacquet modules (Casselman)
items.statement: For an admissible C[U_n]-module π there are canonical isomorphisms π^B ≅ (π_{N_0})^{Z_c} and π^P ≅ (π_{N_P})^{M∩P} (unnormalised Jacquet modules).
items.note: The first is Casselman's Proposition 2.4 (1980); the second follows as in [CT15, Proposition 2.1].

items.name: The Iwahori–Matsumoto presentation of the Hecke algebra of a Tits system
items.statement: For a Tits system (G, B, N) whose Weyl group (W, Σ) is a Coxeter system with q_w = #BwB/B = q^{l(w)}, the convolution algebra H_B of B-biinvariant Z-valued functions is free on the double cosets [BwB] and isomorphic to Z[B_W]/((T_s − 1)(T_s + q) : s ∈ Σ), B_W the braid group, via [BwB] ↦ T_w (Matsumoto 1964).
items.note: Mathlib has CoxeterSystem and its length function (Mathlib/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Basic.lean:157, Mathlib/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Length.lean:75); Tau Ceti has Tits systems and an abstract double-coset Hecke ring (TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/) but not this presentation.

items.name: Proposition 2.2: H_B ≅ H_{B'}, the Iwahori–Hecke algebra of Sp_{2k}
items.statement: Let B' be the Iwahori subgroup of the split group Sp_{2k}(F) and Λ' ≅ Z^k with basis ε'_i = diag(1, …, ϖ², …, ϖ^{−2}, …, 1). The identifications Λ ≅ Λ', W_0 ≅ W'_0 extend to W ≅ W' carrying {s_0, …, s_k} to the simple affine reflections of Sp_{2k}, and induce an isomorphism of Hecke algebras H_B ≅ H_{B'} with [Bε_iB] ↦ [B'ε'_iB'].

items.name: The Bernstein–Lusztig presentation H_{B,C} = H_0 ⊗̃ C[X]
items.statement: With the based root datum of SO_{2k+1}(C) (X = Λ, simple roots ε_i − ε_{i+1}, ε_k), H_{B,C} is the twisted tensor product of H_0 = ⟨T_w : w ∈ W_0⟩ and C[X], with θB_s = B_sθ^s + (θ^s − θ)ζ_β for a simple root β, s = s_β, B_s = T_s − q, where ζ_β = (q − e^β)/(1 − e^β) for β long and (q − e^β)(1 + e^β)/(1 − e^{2β}) otherwise (Lusztig 1989, §3). Its commutative subalgebra O[Λ] acts on Iwahori invariants through the exponents of the Jacquet module.

items.name: The parameter φ_E of Π_E = St_{n−4,E} ⊞ St_{3,E} ⊞ St_{1,E}, exponents, and its L-packet Π_φ
items.statement: For n ≥ 7 let Π_E = St_{n−4,E} ⊞ St_{3,E} ⊞ St_{1,E}, a tempered representation of GL_n(E), with conjugate orthogonal parameter φ_E, and φ its unique extension to a parameter of U_n; Π_φ is the corresponding L-packet. An exponent [m_1, …, m_k] is the character |·|^{m_1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ |·|^{m_k} ⊗ 1 of the torus (E^×)^k × (E^×)^{N=1}; (·)^norm_{N_0} is the normalised Jacquet module for the upper-triangular Borel. f_E ↦ f is the transfer of test functions for stable base change and I_θ: Π_E ≅ Π_E^c the Whittaker-normalised intertwining operator.

items.name: Theorem 2.3(1): the L-packet for n = 7
items.statement: In the setting of item 009, for n = 7, Π_φ has exactly two elements X, Y, characterised by: (a) ⟨tr X + tr Y, f⟩ = ⟨tr Π_E × I_θ, f_E⟩; (b) dim X^P = dim X^B = 1, dim Y^B = 7; (c) X^norm_{N_0} = [1, 0, −1] and (Y^norm_{N_0})^ss = [1, 0, −1] + 2[1, 0, 1] + 4[1, 1, 0].
items.locator: Theorem 2.3, accepted manuscript p. 8; part 1; proved in §3.5, pp. 24–28

items.name: Theorem 2.3(2): the L-packet for n = 9
items.statement: For n = 9, Π_φ is a discrete L-packet with exactly four elements X, Y, Z, W, characterised by: (a) ⟨tr X + tr Y + tr Z + tr W, f⟩ = ⟨tr Π_E × I_θ, f_E⟩; (b) dim X^P = dim X^B = 1, dim Y^B = 11, dim Z^B = 2, dim W^B = 0; (c) X^norm_{N_0} = [2, 1, 0, −1], (Y^norm_{N_0})^ss = [2, 1, 0, −1] + 2[2, 1, 0, 1] + 4[2, 1, 1, 0] + [1, 0, 2, 1] + [1, 2, 0, 1] + 2[1, 2, 1, 0], (Z^norm_{N_0})^ss = [1, 0, 2, 1] + [1, 2, 0, 1].

items.name: Theorem 2.3(3): the L-packets for n = 2k + 1 ≥ 11, inductively
items.statement: For n = 2k + 1 ≥ 11, Π_φ is a discrete L-packet with exactly four elements X_k, Y_k, Z_k, W_k characterised by the trace identity, dim X_k^P = dim X_k^B = 1, dim Y_k^B = dim Y_{k−1}^B + k, dim Z_k^B = dim Z_{k−1}^B + (k − 2), dim W_k^B = 0, and: X_k^norm = [k − 2, k − 3, …, 0, −1]; (Y_k^norm)^ss is the sum of the exponents [1, k − 2, k − 3, …, 1] with 0 inserted as the i-th entry (i = 2, …, k − 1), the exponent 2[1, k − 2, …, 1, 0], and the exponents of Y_{k−1} with k − 2 inserted first; (Z_k^norm)^ss the same without the term 2[1, k − 2, …, 1, 0], with Z_{k−1} in place of Y_{k−1}.

items.name: Theorem 2.4: Kazhdan–Lusztig's Deligne–Langlands classification of tempered Iwahori-spherical representations
items.statement: Let G be a split reductive group over F with connected centre and I an Iwahori subgroup. The tempered irreducible π with π^I ≠ 0 are in natural bijection with Ĝ-conjugacy classes of triples (s, u, ρ): s ∈ Ĝ semisimple in a maximal compact subgroup, u unipotent with sus^{−1} = u^q, and ρ an irreducible representation of M(u, s) = π_0((Z_Ĝ(s) ∩ Z_Ĝ(u))/Z_Ĝ) occurring in H_*(B^s_u, C), B^s_u the variety of Borel subgroups containing s and u. The semisimplified Jacquet module of the representation of (u, s, ρ) is ⊕_α dim Hom_{M(u,s)}(ρ, H_*(B^α, C))·e^α over the M(u, s)-orbits B^α of components of B^s_u.
items.locator: Theorem 2.4, accepted manuscript p. 9; Kazhdan–Lusztig 1987, Theorems 7.12 and 8.2
items.note: A deep theorem (equivariant K-theory of Steinberg varieties); stated as an input. The homology description is in Chriss–Ginzburg, Ch. 8.

items.name: Theorem 2.5: construction of the Iwahori-spherical modules X, Y, Z by Kazhdan–Lusztig
items.statement: For n = 7 there are irreducible admissible C[U_n]-modules X, Y with the dimensions and Jacquet exponents of Theorem 2.3(1)(b)(c); for n = 9 modules X, Y, Z with those of Theorem 2.3(2)(b)(c) (W excluded); and for n = 2k + 1 ≥ 11 modules X_k, Y_k, Z_k with those of Theorem 2.3(3). They are obtained, through Proposition 2.2, from PSp_{2k}(F)-representations attached by Theorem 2.4 to the partition n = (n − 4) + 3 + 1 of the dual SO_{2k+1}(C): M(u, s) = {±1} (n = 7) or {±1}², and B^s_u is paved by affine spaces (De Concini–Lusztig–Procesi; Białynicki-Birula), with the components and exponents listed in the proof.
items.note: For n = 7, B^s_u = X_1 ⊔ X_2 ⊔ X_3 with X_1 two points (exponent [1, 0, −1]), X_2 ≅ P^1 ([1, 0, 1]) and X_3 ≅ P^1 × P^1 ([1, 1, 0]); H_*(B^s_u) is 8-dimensional.

items.name: Proposition 2.6: integral structures with disjoint reductions (q a primitive root mod l)
items.statement: Let l = n − 2 be prime (n ∈ {7, 9}), ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, K/Q_l finite with ring of integers O, residue field k, containing √q, over which X, Y (and Z) are defined. If q is a primitive root modulo l there are H_{B,O}-lattices X^B_O, Y^B_O (and Z^B_O) in X^B_K, Y^B_K (Z^B_K) such that the reductions X^B_O ⊗ k, Y^B_O ⊗ k (and Z^B_O ⊗ k) have pairwise no common Jordan–Hölder factor as H_{B,k}-modules; in fact Y^B_O ⊗ k is absolutely irreducible.
items.locator: Proposition 2.6, accepted manuscript p. 12; Remark 2.7, p. 17
items.note: Y^B_O is given by explicit matrices of T_{s_i} and the ε_i computed with Reeder's Matrices for affine Hecke modules (2000). Remark 2.7: the matrices define Y^B_K without the primitive-root hypothesis; it is needed only for integrality.

items.name: Corollary 2.8: lattices in (X^a ⊕ Y^b ⊕ Z^c)^B split into isotypic parts
items.statement: Let q be a primitive root mod l and M a finite flat H_{B,O}-module with M ⊗ K ≅ (X^B_K)^a ⊕ (Y^B_K)^b (n = 7) or (X^B_K)^a ⊕ (Y^B_K)^b ⊕ (Z^B_K)^c (n = 9). With M_X = M ∩ (X^B_K-isotypic part) and so on, the natural map M_X ⊕ M_Y (⊕ M_Z) → M is an isomorphism.

items.name: Proposition 2.9: the χ̄-localisations when q ≡ −1 mod l
items.statement: Let χ: O[Λ] → O give the action on X^B_K, χ̄ its reduction, and ‖ the anti-involution [BgB] ↦ [Bg^{−1}B]. Suppose q ≡ −1 mod l. Then X^B_K = X^B_K(χ̄) = X^B_K(χ̄‖) and dim_K Y^P_K ∩ Y^B_K(χ̄) = dim_K Y^P_K ∩ Y^B_K(χ̄‖) = 1; and for n = 9 also Z^B_K(χ̄) = 0.

items.name: L-groups of unitary groups, stable and unstable base change of parameters, and bounded parameters
items.statement: For E/F quadratic (local or global) and G = U(n): ᴸG = GL_n(C) ⋊ W_F with c acting by g ↦ Φ_n ᵗg^{−1} Φ_n^{−1}; the L-homomorphism ᴸG → ᴸ(Res_{E/F} G_E), (g, w) ↦ (g, g, w); Φ_bdd(G) the bounded parameters L_F → ᴸG (L_F = W_F or W_F × SU_2(R)). Lemma 3.1: for n odd, φ ↦ φ|_{L_E} is a bijection from Φ_bdd(G) onto the conjugate orthogonal parameters of GL_n(E) (stable base change), and for a character μ of E^× with μ|_{F^×} = ε_{E/F}, φ ↦ φ|_{L_E} ⊗ μ is a bijection onto the conjugate symplectic ones (unstable base change); tempered representations decompose into the L-packets Π_φ (Mœglin, Mok).
items.locator: Lemma 3.1, accepted manuscript p. 19; §§2.2, 3.1, pp. 8, 19; Mok, Lemma 2.2.1
items.note: ML.4 plans Arthur/Mok classification inputs 'with explicit proof-source owners: … packets, multiplicities'.

items.name: The endoscopic group H = U(n − 4) × U(4) and the embedding ξ: ᴸH → ᴸG twisted by μ
items.statement: With m = n − 4 and μ as in Lemma 3.1, ξ sends (g_1, g_2) × 1 to diag(g_1, g_2), 1 × w (w ∈ W_E) to diag(1_m, μ(w)1_4) × w and 1 × w_c to diag(Φ_m, Φ_4)Φ_n^{−1} × w_c (Mínguez); (3.1) is a conjugate form used for the computations.

items.name: Theorem 3.2 (Mœglin, Mok): the L-packet of φ_E has two or four elements
items.statement: The parameter φ_E determines an L-packet Π_φ of tempered representations of G = U_n(F): (i) if m = n − 4 = 3 it has two elements X, Y (the two summands of the reducible n-Ind(St_{3,E} ⊗ 1) from the GL_3(E) × U(1) Levi); (ii) if m ≥ 5 it has four elements X, Y, Z, W in the discrete series. S_φ = π_0(S_φ/{±1}) is {±1} in case (i) and {±1}² in case (ii), paired with Π_φ.
items.locator: Theorem 3.2, accepted manuscript p. 20; Mok, Theorem 2.5.1

items.name: Theorem 3.3 with the signs of the packet: identification of X, Y, Z and their Jacquet modules
items.statement: Suppose E/F ramified and the residue characteristic of F odd. Then the members X, Y (m = 3) or X, Y, Z (m ≥ 5) of Π_φ are semistable with the Jacquet exponents of Theorem 2.3 (for m = 3, X has exponent [1, 0, −1] and Y exponents 4[1, 1, 0] + 2[1, 0, 1] + [1, 0, −1]); W is not semistable. With the characters ε_1, ε_2 of S_φ, the sign ε = ε_1ε_2 satisfies ε(Y) = ε(Z) = 1 and ε(X) = ε(W) = −1, and ε_1(X) = ε_1(Y) = 1, ε_1(Z) = ε_1(W) = −1.
items.locator: Theorem 3.3, accepted manuscript p. 21; sign table p. 21; proof in §3.5, pp. 24–28
items.note: Corrected for source issue E3: part (i) prints the exponent of X as [1, 0, 1]. The proof compares the stable identity and the endoscopic identity Σ ε(π)⟨tr π, f⟩ = ⟨tr π_H, f^H⟩ ((3.7)) on the maximal split torus, using Lemma 3.6 and Proposition 3.7.

items.name: Lemma 3.4: a conjugate-symplectic Hecke character μ with prescribed archimedean components
items.statement: For a CM extension E/F of a totally real field there is a continuous μ: E^×\A_E^× → C^× with μ|_{A_F^×} = ε_{E/F} and μ(z) = (z/z̄)^{1/2} for z ∈ E_w ≅ C at every archimedean place w.

items.name: Theorem 3.5 (Mok): multiplicity formula for the quasi-split unitary group and the endoscopic datum (Π_m, Π_4 ⊗ μ)
items.statement: Let Π_m, Π_4 be conjugate self-dual cuspidal representations of GL_m(A_E), GL_4(A_E) with the archimedean parameters of §3.3, so that (Π_m, Π_4 ⊗ μ) is a tempered Arthur parameter ψ for the quasi-split G* = U(n) with S_ψ = {±1} ∋ s. For local π_v ∈ Π_{φ_v}, almost all unramified, π = ⊗π_v occurs in L²_cusp(G*(F)\G*(A)) if and only if ∏_v ⟨s, π_v⟩ = 1, and then with multiplicity one.
items.locator: Theorem 3.5, accepted manuscript p. 22; Mok, Theorem 2.5.2
items.note: Mok's results are conditional on the stabilisation of the twisted trace formula (Mœglin–Waldspurger); cuspidality follows because residual representations are nowhere tempered (Clozel 1993).

items.name: Arthur's stabilisation of the trace formula for G* and G, and the reduction to the endoscopic data (G*, H)
items.statement: I^{G*}_disc(f*) = Σ_E ι(G*, E) S^E_disc(f*^E) (3.12) and T^G_disc(f) = I^G_disc(f) = Σ_E ι(G, E) S^E_disc(f^E) (3.13) (Arthur 2003, 2005); by Labesse's CM base change for stable discrete terms and Jacquet–Shalika disjointness (the argument of Clozel–Harris–Labesse 2011, Lemma 4.2), after isolating the Hecke eigenvalues of σ_1 ⊞ σ_2 or π only E = G* and E = H contribute.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.8, (3.12)–(3.13), accepted manuscript pp. 29–31
items.note: ET.4 plans the simple stable and twisted unitary trace formulas and ET.7 the unitary-to-GL base-change identities; ML.4 the stabilisation inputs.

items.name: Transfer factors on maximally split tori, and Lemma 3.6
items.statement: At a p-adic place, ∆_0 = ∆_I∆_II∆_III,1∆_III,2∆_IV with ∆_I = ∆_III,1 = 1 (H^1(F, T_sc) = 1), ∆_II = 1 for trivial a- and χ-data, ∆_IV = D_G(t)/D_H(t_H); and (Lemma 3.6) for associated t ∈ T_G and t_H = (t_0, z_1, z_2) ∈ T_H ⊂ U(m) × U(4), ∆(t_H, t) = μ(z_1)μ(z_2)∆_IV(t_H, t). At archimedean places Kottwitz's factor equals ±∆_0, the sign cancelling when [F:Q] is even.
items.note: Langlands–Shelstad transfer factors are planned in EndoscopicTransfer ET.1; the explicit computation for this embedding ξ is not.

items.name: Proposition 3.7 (Mœglin): a Jacquet module exponent of the endoscopic packet
items.statement: The Jacquet module of π_H contains μ(z)^{−1}[2, 1, 0, −1] with multiplicity 2. More generally, for n = a + b with a ≤ b odd and π the L-packet of St_{a,E} ⊞ St_{b,E}, the full Jacquet module contains μ^{−1}[(b − 1)/2, (b − 3)/2, …, (1 − a)/2].
items.note: Proved by Mœglin's hereditary formula for Jacquet modules, as in [CT15, Appendix A].

items.name: Theorem 3.8(1): automorphic representations of the definite unitary group with endoscopic base change
items.statement: Let G be the unitary group in n = l + 2 variables over F (l > 5 prime), split by the CM field E, compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, [F:Q] even. Let σ_1, σ_2 be conjugate self-dual cuspidal representations of GL_4(A_E), GL_m(A_E) with (a) σ_1 ⊞ σ_2 regular algebraic of infinity type ((l + 1)/2, (l − 1)/2, …, (−1 − l)/2) at every infinite place and ∏_{v|∞} det(w_v) = 1; (b) places v_0, …, v_s ramified in E of odd residue characteristic with σ_{1,w_i} ≅ St_3 ⊞ St_1, σ_{2,w_i} ≅ St_m; (c) every other ramified place of σ_1 ⊞ σ_2 split over F, and no other place of F ramified in E. Then there are exactly 4^{s+1}/2 automorphic representations σ of G(A_F) with stable base change σ_1 ⊞ σ_2, each of multiplicity one, in bijection with the tuples (σ_{v_i}) ∈ ∏ Π_{φ_{v_i}} with ∏ ε_{v_i}(σ_{v_i}) = 1.
items.locator: Theorem 3.8, accepted manuscript p. 28; part 1; Remark 3.9, p. 29
items.note: Remark 3.9: ∏ det(w_v) = 1 holds if every place above l splits in E with [F_v : Q_l] even and σ_1 ⊞ σ_2 is ι-ordinary ([CT14, Lemma 2.6]); equivalently a Shelstad sign.

items.name: Theorem 3.8(2): the same count for a cuspidal base change, and strong stable base change for G
items.statement: Let π be a RACSDC representation of GL_n(A_E) regular algebraic of the same infinity type with π_{w_i} ≅ St_m ⊞ St_3 ⊞ St_1 at places v_0, …, v_s as in Theorem 3.8(1) and the same splitting conditions. Then there are exactly 4^{s+1} automorphic representations of G(A_F) with stable base change π, each of multiplicity one, in bijection with ∏ Π_{φ_{v_i}}. Moreover every automorphic representation σ of G(A_F) whose Galois representation is irreducible or has constituents of dimensions (4, m) has a strong stable base change to GL_n(A_E) with the local components predicted at every place.
items.locator: Theorem 3.8, accepted manuscript p. 28; part 2 and pp. 30–31

items.name: Theorem 3.10: the case l = 5 (n = 7)
items.statement: For n = 7, with σ_1, σ_2 of GL_4, GL_3 (σ_{2,w_i} ≅ St_3), the same hypotheses and the two-element packets {X_v, Y_v} (ε(X_v) = −1, ε(Y_v) = 1): there are exactly 2^s automorphic representations of G(A_F) with stable base change σ_1 ⊞ σ_2, in bijection with the tuples with ∏ ε = 1; and exactly 2^{s+1} with a cuspidal base change π with π_{w_i} ≅ St_3 ⊞ St_3 ⊞ St_1; stable base change holds.

items.name: The level-raising set-up of §4.1: fields, places, the definite unitary group and the endoscopic datum
items.statement: Let l ≥ 5 be prime, ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, E a CM field with maximal totally real subfield F such that every place v | l of F splits in E with [F_v : Q_l] even, and places v_0, …, v_s (s ≥ 1) of F ramified in E of odd residue characteristic with q_{v_0} ≡ −1 mod l and each q_{v_i} (i ≥ 1) a primitive root mod l, every other place unramified in E. Let n = l + 2, m = l − 2 and G the unitary group in n variables split by E, compact at infinity and quasi-split at every finite place. Let π_1, π_2 be cuspidal conjugate self-dual representations of GL_m(A_E), GL_4(A_E) with π_{1,w_i} ≅ St_m, π_{2,w_i} ≅ St_3 ⊞ St_1, other ramification split over F; π = π_1 ⊞ π_2 regular algebraic, ι-ordinary of infinity type ((n − 1)/2, …, (1 − n)/2); r̄_ι(π) = ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2 with ρ̄_i absolutely irreducible of dimensions m and 4; ρ̄_1(t_{w_i}) regular unipotent and ρ̄_2(t_{w_i}) of Jordan type 3 + 1 for a generator t_{w_i} of tame inertia.

items.name: Algebraic modular forms S(U, A) on the definite unitary group, their Hecke algebras T(U, O), ordinary parts and the maximal ideals m, m^∨
items.statement: For an open compact U ⊂ G(A_F^∞) and an O-algebra A, S(U, A) is the space of functions G(F)\G(A_F^∞)/U → A (weight zero). With the integral model, identifications ι_w: G(F_v) ≅ GL_n(E_w) at split places and uniformisers at places above l of [CT15, §3.3], the Hecke algebra T(U, O) ⊂ End_O(S(U, O)) is generated by the unramified operators at split places of maximal level and the operators U_v^j at v | l. An automorphic Σ with trivial Σ_∞ contributes to N ⊂ S(U, O) if N ∩ ι^{−1}Σ^{∞,U,ord} ≠ 0. Levels: U_{0,v_0} = P_{v_0}, U_{0,v_i} = B_{v_i} (i ≥ 1), hyperspecial at inert places, Iw(c) at places above l, U_0 sufficiently small with σ^{U_0} ≠ 0; U_1 equals U_0 except U_{1,v_0} = B_{v_0}, so [U_0 : U_1] = q_{v_0} + 1. m ⊂ T(U_1, O) is the maximal ideal of σ and m^∨ that of σ^∨.
items.note: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.5 plans the identification of algebraic modular forms on compact-at-infinity groups with functions on finite adelic double cosets; the Hecke algebras and ordinary parts on definite unitary groups are in the Part II PolarizedAutomorphyLifting proposed by the Boxer–Calegari–Gee extraction (not yet in the atlas).

items.name: Proposition 4.1: the local types of automorphic representations contributing to S(U_1, O)_m
items.statement: If Σ contributes to S(U_1, O)_m and Π is its stable base change to GL_n(A_E) (a RACSD representation), then Π is ι-ordinary and either (1) Π_{w_i} ≅ St_m ⊞ St_3 ⊞ St_1 for every i = 0, …, s, or (2) for some i, r_ι(Π)(t_{w_i}) has Jordan decomposition of partition n = (n − 2) + 1 + 1 or n = n, and Π is cuspidal.
items.note: The proof corrects the proof of [CT15, Lemma 4.3] (semistability of Π_w) and uses the closure order on nilpotent classes (dim ker N^j ≤ dim ker N̄^j), the parity condition of Mok's Lemma 2.2.1, and quadratic characters ≡ 1 mod λ.

items.name: Proposition 4.3: the perfect pairing on S(U_1) and its vanishing on S(U_0) mod l
items.statement: The pairing ⟨f, g⟩ = Σ_{x ∈ G(F)\G(A^∞_F)/U_1} f(x)g(x) on S(U_1, O) satisfies ⟨af, g⟩ = ⟨f, a^‖g⟩ for a ∈ H_{B_{v_0},O} and induces (1) perfect pairings S(U_1, O)_m × S(U_1, O)_{m^∨} → O and S(U_1, k)_m × S(U_1, k)_{m^∨} → k; (2) a pairing vanishing on S(U_0, k)_m × S(U_0, k)_{m^∨} (because q_{v_0} ≡ −1 mod l); (3) a perfect pairing M × N → O whose reduction vanishes on M^{U_0} ⊗ k × N^{U_0} ⊗ k, for the isotypic submodules M, N of the proof of Theorem 4.2.
items.locator: Proposition 4.3, accepted manuscript p. 36; as in [CT15, Proposition 4.5]

items.name: Lemma 4.4: the structure of M as an H_{B_{v_0}}-module
items.statement: Under the hypothesis (⋆) of the proof of Theorem 4.2, M ⊗_{O,ι} C ≅ (X^{B_{v_0}}_{v_0})^a ⊕ (Y^{B_{v_0}}_{v_0})^b ⊕ (Z^{B_{v_0}}_{v_0})^c ≅ N ⊗_{O,ι} C as H_{B_{v_0},C}-modules, with a > b = c ≥ 0.
items.note: Endoscopic (non-cuspidal) base changes contribute only X at v_0, cuspidal ones X, Y and Z; the endoscopic set is non-empty because of the initial datum π_1 ⊞ π_2.

items.name: Theorem 4.2: level-raising for l = 5 and l = 7
items.statement: In the set-up of §4.1 with l = 5 or l = 7, there is an automorphic representation Σ of G(A_F) contributing to S(U_1, O)_m that falls into case 2 of Proposition 4.1: its base change is cuspidal and at some w_i the monodromy has Jordan type (n − 2) + 1 + 1 or n.
items.locator: Theorem 4.2, accepted manuscript p. 35; proof pp. 35–37; Remark 4.5
items.note: Proof by contradiction: choosing R_i with ∏ ε_{v_i}(R_i) = −1 (i ≥ 1), the P_{v_0}-fixed part M_1 of M(χ̄) has rank a + b (Proposition 2.9) and is isotropic mod l, while M(χ̄) has rank a + 3b (X has one exponent ≡ [2, 1, 0, −1], Y three, Z none, as q_{v_0} ≡ −1 mod l); so 2(a + b) ≤ a + 3b, contradicting a > b. Remark 4.5: the count fails for l > 7 since Z(χ̄) ≠ 0.

items.name: Local deformation problems at places of L^+: ordinary, unrestricted, R^χ_v, R^St_v, and the new partition rings R^m_v
items.statement: For v ∈ T_L: R^Δ_v the ordinary lifting ring (v | l; Geraghty, [Tho15, §3.3.2]); R_v the unrestricted ring (v ∈ S_{a,L}, formally smooth, unramified universal lift); for v ∤ l with q_v ≡ 1 mod l and characters χ_{v,i}: O^×_{L_ṽ} → O^× trivial mod λ, R^{χ_v}_v classifying lifts whose inertia has characteristic polynomial ∏(X − χ_{v,i}) (R^1_v when all are trivial); R^St_v classifying unipotently ramified lifts with Frobenius eigenvalues α, q_vα, …, q_v^{n−1}α; and, for a partition m = (m_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ m_k) of n, R^m_v, the maximal O-flat reduced quotient of R^1_v classifying lifts for which a lift of Frob_ṽ^{−1} has characteristic polynomial in Taylor's scheme Pol_n(m, q_v) (so R^{(n)}_v = R^St_v).
items.note: The first four are planned in LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 ('semistable, Steinberg and minimally ramified analogues away from p for rank n') and R08.2; R^m_v is new here. A local deformation problem is determined by its ring (Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor, Lemma 3.2).

items.name: Lemma 5.2: R^1_v[1/l] is smooth at pure points of R^m_v, with a unique minimal prime there
items.statement: Let x ∈ Spec R^m_v[1/l] be a closed point given by ρ: G_{L_ṽ} → GL_n(O) with ρ ⊗ Q̄_l pure (Taylor–Yoshida, Lemma 1.4). Then Spec R^1_v[1/l] is formally smooth over K at x, there is a unique minimal prime Q_v of R^1_v in the kernel of R^1_v → O, and Q_v contains ker(R^1_v → R^m_v).
items.note: Uses that (R^1_v)^red is O-flat equidimensional of dimension 1 + n² (Taylor 2008, Proposition 3.1; Thorne 2012, Lemma 3.15) and that Spec R_v[1/l] is equidimensional of dimension n² and smooth at pure points (BLGGT14, Lemma 1.3.2).

items.name: Deformation data D = (L, {R_v}) and the attached objects of [Tho15]: Λ_L, S({R_v}), U, S_D, T_D, R_D, P_D, J_D, R^red_D
items.statement: For a good soluble CM extension L/E (every place of V_0 ∪ S_a split), a set R of places of L^+ above T ∖ (S_l ∪ S_a) and local rings R_v of types 3–5: the Iwasawa algebra Λ_L = ⊗̂_{v∈S_{l,L}} O⟦(I_{L_ṽ}(l)^{ab})^n⟧; the global deformation problem S({R_v}) of type (L/L^+, R ∪ S_{l,L} ∪ S_{a,L}, …, Λ_L, r̄, ε^{1−n}δ^n_{L/L^+}, {R^Δ_v} ∪ {R_v}); the level U; the space of modular forms S_D = S_χ(U(l^∞), K/O)^∨, finite free over Λ_L; the Hecke algebra T_D localised at the maximal ideal of a descent of Π_0; the universal deformation ring R_D ⊃ the universal pseudodeformation ring P_D (finite); a surjection P_D → T_D with kernel I_D and J_D = I_D R_D when every R_v is some R^{χ_v}_v; and the reducible quotient R^red_D. T_D is finite torsion-free over Λ_L, and when every R_v is R^{χ_v}_v or R^St_v each minimal prime of R_D has dimension ≥ 1 + n[L^+ : Q].
items.note: From Thorne, Automorphy lifting for residually reducible l-adic Galois representations (JAMS 2015), Propositions 3.8, 3.9, 3.29, 4.3, Definitions 3.27, 3.31, 4.2; the group 𝒢_n of Clozel–Harris–Taylor §2.1. A prerequisite paper; not planned in the atlas (GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 plans polarized deformation problems, but not pseudodeformations of reducible r̄).

items.name: Thorne's R = T and automorphy lifting for residually reducible representations (inputs from [Tho15])
items.statement: (1) [Tho15, Theorem 4.19, Corollary 4.20]: under hypotheses (1)–(5) there, for a minimal prime Q_1 ⊂ R_{D_1} inside a suitable prime, J_{D_1} ⊂ Q_1 and R_{D_1}/Q_1 is finite over Λ_L of dimension dim Λ_L. (2) [Tho15, Theorem 7.1]: automorphy lifting for ρ̄ = ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2 Schur, ordinary, given an automorphic ordinary lift that is Steinberg at some place. (3) [Tho15, Lemmas 1.9, 3.36, Corollary 4.14, Proposition 4.18]: dimension-one primes avoiding countably many small quotients, twisting by ∆/(c + 1), and soluble base change of Hecke algebras. (4) Hida classicality for GL_n over CM fields (Geraghty, Lemma 2.6.4).
items.locator: Proofs of Lemmas 5.3–5.6, Theorems 5.1 and 5.7, accepted manuscript pp. 40–44
items.note: Stated inputs from Thorne 2015 and Geraghty's preprint; prerequisites. The Boxer–Calegari–Gee extraction's proposed Part II PolarizedAutomorphyLifting plans Thorne 2012/2017 and BLGGT14 but not Thorne 2015.

items.name: Lemma 5.3: dimension of the reducible locus with Steinberg-type conditions
items.statement: Fix a partition m with m_1 > n_1 = dim ρ̄_1 and a deformation datum D = (L, {R_v}_{v∈R_0} ∪ {R^m_v}_{v∈R_1}). Let ∆ (resp. ∆') be the Galois group of the maximal abelian l-extension of L unramified outside l (resp. in addition split at R̃_1 ∪ R̃^c_1) and d = dim_{Q_l} ker(∆ ⊗ Q_l → ∆' ⊗ Q_l)^{c=−1}. Then dim R^red_D ≤ 1 + n[L^+ : Q] − d and R^red_D is finite over Λ_L.
items.note: The key point: a reducible deformation (r̄_1 ⊗ Ψ_1) ⊕ (r̄_2 ⊗ Ψ_2) of type R^m_v forces Ψ_1(Frob_ṽ) = Ψ_2(Frob_ṽ), since m_1 > n_1 > n_2. Uses the potential ordinary automorphy of ρ̄_1, ρ̄_2 (hypothesis 4 of Theorem 5.1).

items.name: Lemma 5.4: dim R_D/J_{D'}R_D = dim Λ_L for the partition of the monodromy at w_0
items.statement: Let D = (L, {R^{χ_v}_v}_{v∈R_0} ∪ {R^m_v}_{v∈R_1}) with m the Jordan type of N, rec^T(Π_{w_0}) = (r, N), R_1 the places above v_0, and D' = (L, {R^{χ_v}_v}_{v∈R_0} ∪ {R^1_v}_{v∈R_1}). Then dim R_D/J_{D'}R_D = dim Λ_L.

items.name: Lemma 5.5: changing the characters χ_v after a soluble base change
items.statement: Let D_0^χ = (L_0, {R^{χ_v}_v}_{v∈R}) with pairwise distinct χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n} for each v ∈ R, and L ⊃ L_0 good with every χ_{v,i} trivial on inertia of L above R. For D = (L, ∅) there is a commutative diagram R_D ← P_D → T_D over R^nil_{D_0^χ} ← P^nil_{D_0^χ} → T_{D_0^χ}.
items.note: Uses soluble base change and descent for G ([CT14, Proposition 2.9]); this is why n_1 ≠ n_2 and n_1n_2 even are assumed.

items.name: Lemma 5.6: a characteristic-l prime of R_D containing J_D yields a Steinberg automorphic lift
items.statement: Suppose a deformation datum D = (L, ∅) and a dimension-one prime 𝔭 ⊂ R_D of characteristic l satisfy: (1) r_𝔭: G_L → GL_n(Frac A) is absolutely irreducible (A the normalisation of R_D/𝔭); (2) the characters ψ^v_1, …, ψ^v_n of I_{L_ṽ} (v ∈ S_{l,L}) are pairwise distinct; (3) some σ ∈ I_{L_ṽ} has eigenvalues satisfying no non-trivial Z-linear relation; (4) J_D ⊂ 𝔭; (5) r_𝔭|_{G_{L_ũ}} is trivial for some u ∈ T_L ∖ (S_{l,L} ∪ S_{a,L}). Then there is an ι-ordinary RACSDC Π_1 of GL_n(A_L) with r̄_ι(Π_1) ≅ r̄_ι(Π)|_{G_L} and Π_{1,ũ} an unramified twist of Steinberg.

items.name: Theorem 5.1: level-raising to Steinberg for residually reducible representations
items.statement: Let E be CM, Π a RACSDC representation of GL_n(A_E) with r̄_ι(Π) = ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2, ρ̄_i absolutely irreducible, non-isomorphic, ρ̄_i^c ≅ ρ̄_i^∨ ε^{1−n}, n_1 > n_2, r̄_ι(Π) primitive, and a place w_0 where Π_{w_0} is Iwahori-spherical and N in rec^T(Π_{w_0}) = (r, N) has a Jordan block of length > n_1. Assume (1) Π is ι-ordinary; (2) l > 3, l ∤ n_1, n_2, n, and n_1n_2 even; (3) each ρ̄_i|_{G_{E(ζ_l)}} is adequate and E(ζ_l) ⊄ the fixed field of ad r̄_ι(Π); (4) a CM E_0/E linearly disjoint from the field cut out by ρ̄ and ι-ordinary RAECSDC (π_i, χ_i) of GL_{n_i}(A_{E_0}) with r̄_ι(π_i) ≅ ρ̄_i|_{G_{E_0}}. Then there are a soluble CM E_1/E linearly disjoint from the extension of E(ζ_l) cut out by r̄_ι(Π) and an ι-ordinary RACSDC Π_1 of GL_n(A_{E_1}) with r̄_ι(Π_1) ≅ r̄_ι(Π)|_{G_{E_1}} and Π_{1,w_1} an unramified twist of Steinberg at a place w_1 | w_0.
items.locator: Theorem 5.1, accepted manuscript p. 37; proof pp. 38–43

items.name: Theorem 5.7: automorphy lifting for residually reducible ρ from a lift with a large Jordan block
items.statement: Let E be CM and ρ: G_E → GL_n(Q̄_l) continuous with (1) ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ε^{1−n}; (2) finitely many ramified places; (3) ρ ordinary of weight λ ([Tho15, Definition 2.5]); (4) l > 3 and E(ζ_l) ⊄ the field cut out by ad ρ̄; (5) ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2 with ρ̄_i|_{G_{E(ζ_l)}} adequate, n_1 ≠ n_2, n_1n_2 even, l ∤ n_1n_2(n_1 + n_2), ρ̄ primitive; (6) a place w_0 ∤ l with ρ|^ss_{G_{E_{w_0}}} ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^n ψε^{n−i}, ψ unramified; (7) an ι-ordinary RACSDC Π with r̄_ι(Π) ≅ ρ̄ whose N at w_0 has a Jordan block of length > max(n_1, n_2); (8) as hypothesis 4 of Theorem 5.1. Then ρ ≅ r_ι(π) for a RACSDC automorphic representation π of GL_n(A_E).
items.note: Combines Theorem 5.1 with [Tho15, Theorem 7.1] and soluble descent; the paper offers it for use elsewhere.

items.name: The congruence Sym^{l+1} r̄ ≅ (φr̄ ⊗ r̄) ⊕ χ² Sym^{l−3} r̄ for two-dimensional mod l representations
items.statement: For a two-dimensional representation r̄ with values in GL_2(F̄_l), determinant χ and φ the (arithmetic) Frobenius acting on coefficients, (Sym^{l+1} r̄)^ss ≅ (φr̄ ⊗ r̄) ⊕ χ² Sym^{l−3} r̄, by the representation theory of GL_2(F_l); if the image of r̄ is large both summands are irreducible, of dimensions 4 and l − 2.
items.locator: (1.1), accepted manuscript p. 2; proof of Theorem 6.2, p. 45

items.name: Known functorial transfers used: Gelbart–Jacquet, Kim–Shahidi, Kim, Ramakrishnan and Arthur–Clozel
items.statement: (1) Sym² π exists for cuspidal π of GL_2(A_F) and is cuspidal iff π is not automorphically induced from a quadratic extension iff π ≇ π ⊗ η for all non-trivial Hecke characters η (Gelbart–Jacquet; Theorem 7.3(1)); if Sym² π is cuspidal, π_E and Sym² π_E stay cuspidal after any quadratic base change (Arthur–Clozel, Theorem 3.4.2; Theorem 7.3(2)). (2) Sym³ π (Kim–Shahidi) and Sym⁴ π (Kim) exist. (3) Ramakrishnan's Theorem M: the Rankin–Selberg product of two cuspidal representations of GL_2 is automorphic on GL_4.
items.locator: Theorem 7.3, accepted manuscript p. 47; proof of Theorem 6.2, p. 46; Corollary 7.2(1)
items.note: ML.5 plans to 'register cyclic base change, automorphic induction and selected tensor/symmetric-power transfers with exact hypotheses'.

items.name: Change of weight and base-change inputs from [CT14], [CT15] and [CHT08]
items.statement: (1) [CT15, Proposition 3.10] with base change for U_2: a RACSDC π'_2 of GL_2(A_{E_2}), ι-ordinary with HT_τ = {(1 − l)/2, (1 + l)/2}, π'_{2,z_i} ≅ St_2 ⊗ ιω (ω the Teichmüller lift of ε̄^{(l−1)/2}), r̄_ι(π'_2) ≅ ε̄^{(l−1)/2} ⊗ ρ̄_2, ramified only above split places. (2) [CT14, Lemma 2.6] (ι-ordinarity of Π_1 ⊞ Π_2; the signs det(w_v)) and [CT14, Proposition 2.9] (soluble base change and descent for G). (3) [CHT08, Lemma 4.1.4]: a finite-order ψ: G_E → Q̄_l^× unramified above u_0 with ψψ^c = r_ι(χ)|_{G_E}.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.2, accepted manuscript pp. 45–46; Remark 3.9; Lemma 5.5
items.note: Stated inputs from the earlier papers of the series (Compositio 2014, Annals 2015) and Clozel–Harris–Taylor; prerequisites. The proof of Theorem 6.1 also follows 'a series of reductions … essentially the same as those of [CT15, §6]'.

items.name: Theorem 6.2: Sym^{l+1} ρ is automorphic for l ∈ {5, 7} under ordinarity and Steinberg hypotheses
items.statement: Let l ∈ {5, 7}, F totally real, ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, and (π, χ) a RAESDC representation of GL_2(A_F) with (1) π ι-ordinary of weight zero (infinity type (1/2, −1/2) at every real place); (2) ρ̄ = r̄_ι(π) irreducible with image containing a conjugate of SL_2(F_{l^a}) for some a > 1, and (φρ̄ ⊗ ρ̄)|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} and (Sym^{l−3} ρ̄)|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} adequate; (3) a place u_0 ∤ 2 with π_{u_0} an unramified twist of Steinberg, q_{u_0} a primitive root mod l and ρ̄ ramified at u_0. Then Sym^{l+1} ρ is automorphic.
items.note: Proof: pass to a CM field E_2 with places above u_0 ramified in E_2/F_2 (q ≡ −1 at one, primitive roots at the others), build Π_1 ⊞ Π_2 of type (4, l − 2) with the congruence of item 046, apply Theorem 4.2 and then Theorem 5.7, and descend. Corrected for source issue E4 (E_2 = F_2·E_1).

items.name: Theorem 6.1 (Theorem 1.1): the 6th and 8th symmetric powers
items.statement: Let F be totally real and (π, χ) a RAESDC representation of GL_2(A_F) not automorphically induced from a quadratic CM extension. (1) If F ∩ Q(ζ_5) = Q, the 6th symmetric power lift of π exists as a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_7(A_F). (2) If F ∩ Q(ζ_7) = Q, the 8th symmetric power lift exists as a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_9(A_F).
items.locator: Theorem 6.1, accepted manuscript p. 44; Theorem 1.1, p. 2
items.note: Deduced from Theorem 6.2 by the reductions of [CT15, §6]. Superseded in range, by a different method, by Newton–Thorne (PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21, -21-B, -26); ML.3 should keep the hypotheses of each source.

items.name: Theorem 7.1: reduction of the mixed-parity case to the RAESDC case
items.statement: Let F be totally real and r ≥ 1. Suppose that for every RAESDC (π, χ) of GL_2(A_F) not automorphically induced from a quadratic CM extension there is a RAESDC (Π, Ξ) of GL_{r+1}(A_F) with Sym^r rec_{F_v}(π_v) ≅ rec_{F_v}(Π_v) at all finite v. Then for every cuspidal π of GL_2(A_F) with π_∞ essentially square-integrable and not automorphically induced from a quadratic CM extension there is a cuspidal Π of GL_{r+1}(A_F) with Sym^r rec_{F_v}(π_v) ≅ rec_{F_v}(Π_v) at all finite v; in particular L(Sym^r π, s) = L(Π, s) continues to an entire function with the expected functional equation.
items.note: Mixed-parity π become algebraic up to twist after base change to a CM field (Blasius–Rogawski).

items.name: Corollary 7.2 (with Corollaries 1.2 and 1.3): symmetric powers up to 8
items.statement: Let F be totally real and π cuspidal on GL_2(A_F) with π_∞ essentially square-integrable, not automorphically induced from a quadratic CM extension. There is a cuspidal Π of GL_{r+1}(A_F) with Sym^r rec_{F_v}(π_v) ≅ rec_{F_v}(Π_v) at all finite v in each case: (1) F arbitrary, 1 ≤ r ≤ 4; (2) F ∩ Q(ζ_5) = Q, r ∈ {5, 6}; (3) F ∩ Q(ζ_35) = Q, r = 7; (4) F ∩ Q(ζ_7) = Q, r = 8. Hence L(Sym^r π, s) is entire with the expected functional equation (Corollary 1.3).
items.locator: Corollary 7.2, accepted manuscript p. 46; Corollaries 1.2–1.3, p. 2
items.note: Cases r = 5, 7 are [CT15, Theorem 1.2]; r ≤ 4 are Gelbart–Jacquet, Kim–Shahidi and Kim.

items.name: Lemma 7.4: twisting π_E to a RACSDC representation
items.statement: Let F be totally real, π cuspidal on GL_2(A_F) with π_∞ essentially square-integrable, and E/F an imaginary CM extension with π_E cuspidal. Then there is a continuous character χ: E^×\A_E^× → C^× with π_E ⊗ χ RACSDC.
items.note: Uses Chevalley's congruence subgroup theorem for units (to make the central character finite order) and [CHT08, Lemma 4.1.4].

items.name: Lemma 7.5: large residual image for a density-one set of primes
items.statement: Let E be imaginary CM and π a RACSDC representation of GL_2(A_E) with Sym² π cuspidal. Then there is a set L of rational primes of Dirichlet density 1 such that for all l ∈ L and all ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, r̄_ι(π) is irreducible with image containing a conjugate of SL_2(F_l).
items.note: Uses BLGGT14 Theorem 5.5.2 and Proposition 5.3.2, Fontaine–Laffaille's description of r̄_ι(π)|_{I_v} for l large (so that α_2/α_1 has order > 5), and the classification of finite subgroups of PGL_2(F̄_l).

items.name: Potential diagonalisability and automorphy inputs from Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor
items.statement: [BLGGT14, Theorem 4.4.1]: an odd irreducible R̄: G_F → GL_2(F̄_l) with suitable large image has a potentially diagonalisable lift, unramified almost everywhere; [BLGGT14, Lemma 1.4.3]: potential diagonalisability is preserved by restriction; [BLGGT14, Theorem 4.2.1]: automorphy lifting for potentially diagonalisable, residually (potentially diagonalisably) automorphic representations with adequate residual image; [BLGGT14, Theorem 5.5.2, Proposition 5.3.2]: irreducibility of r_ι(π) and Sym² r_ι(π) and of their reductions for a density-one set of l.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 7.5 and Proposition 7.6, accepted manuscript pp. 48–49
items.note: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 assembles potential automorphy from these theorems; the Boxer–Calegari–Gee extraction's proposed PolarizedAutomorphyLifting plans other parts of BLGGT14 (§2 and Appendix A).

items.name: Proposition 7.6: symmetric powers over a CM field from those over its totally real subfield
items.statement: Let E/F be an imaginary CM quadratic extension and r ≥ 1. If Sym^r r_ι(π) is automorphic for every RAESDC (π, χ) of GL_2(A_F) not automorphically induced from a CM extension, then Sym^r r_ι(Π) is automorphic for every RACSDC Π of GL_2(A_E) not automorphically induced from a quadratic extension.
items.note: Proof: by Lemma 7.5 pick l > 2(r + 2) with large residual image; extend r̄_ι(Π) ⊗ φ to an odd R̄ of G_F; lift R̄ potentially diagonalisably (BLGGT14 Theorem 4.4.1); R is automorphic and Sym^r r_ι(Π) is residually potentially diagonalisably automorphic, hence automorphic (BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1). Corrected for source issue E5.
